title: How he produces vibrato: lip, hand and horn shake
summary: He explains lip trills and the shaking horn, and the trombone players he copied.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Lips, teeth and breath: the physical craft of brass playing

blocks.x: Well do you use lip or diaphragm or something?

Well I can get it from the lip but I use the hand, but not too much hand. I got a way of getting the vibrato by just shaking my horn, you know, and getting in a certain position. It's just about shaking it like this I get it, instead of all the way, like this. You can move the whole horn.
I got this from Dutre and Roy, you know, like this, the vibrato.
Yeah. But now, but now I use a little lip and I just can shake it like this and I can enrich my tone. Just shake it like that.
Well sometimes it sounds like you're using lip trills like T-Garden would.
Well I do, I use a lot of, I'd say about sixty, seventy percent of my working jazz is lip trills. Yeah, lip trills. I use a lot of lip trills.
Do you go down into, well you know Roy always said he could play his horn backwards. Yeah. In the six and seven position, do you use that? Or do you go down first and second?

Well I tell you, Claude Jones I think was one of the great trombones, used to be the Fletcher Anderson. Claude, I noticed this playing Dickie Wells and all them fellas. See I always go, whenever this fella was in town, I'd go there, as I said before. And I tried to, I copied, I'm a copycat, see what I'm talking about? And I'd go back home and work on it. Now some leaders don't like much vibrato. You suppose if you're in a section, I mean you suppose a match of tones, you understand what I'm talking about? So Roy, oh yeah when it comes to these, like that low E natural down in the seventh position, well that don't require too much vibrato. The pretty notes are, the notes are in the staff and as high as like G, F and like that, you know, and the B flat and C and things like that. But down there, they always want me to just give them a big tone down there, you know, and a lift and that E natural down there, you see. And so, and that's what I've been trying to do. See I practice every day here in Chicago, an hour and a half, two hours a day. I'm striving now more harder than I did earlier, see what I'm talking about? Because I'm beginning to become a little more recognized now. You see I'm getting in demand, I'd say, that's why I'm down here I figure, because somebody spoke for me, you understand? And if I wasn't producing, they wouldn't speak for you, you understand what I'm talking about? But you'll find out that it's going to be a little different when I play tonight. It's going to be, some of this fellow here, I'm not so great that I didn't hear him and couldn't like him, or the German, I like both of them. It's only the 40, well I imagine it's kind of by the way it's like, you understand what I'm talking about? But they both have nice big tones, you know? And so that's what I love, is a nice tone.
